Three second-hand graphics cards sit in a tower under a desk. Each one holds eight gigabytes of memory, which is not very much, and none of them are connected to each other by anything faster than the motherboard. For two years, that was enough to run other people's models badly. It is now enough to run them well, and the difference was never the hardware.
